title: Why I Spent 500 Stack Overflow Reputation Points on One Question
description: Find out how building reputation points on Stack Overflow could benefit you and your team when searching for solutions to difficult or rare issues. I discuss how offering bounty points for a problem can attract eyes of developers who may have more experience in the nuances that are attached to the issue you are facing.   About SO: https://stackoverflow.com/company  How to ask a good question: https://stackoverflow.com/help/how-to-ask  How to write a good answer: https://stackoverflow.com/help/how-to-answer  ChromeDev Tools: https://developers.google.com/web/tools/chrome-devtools/  Support the channel: https://paypal.me/codingwithabdullah FB: https://www.facebook.com/codingwithabdullah Twitter: https://twitter.com/ai_rasheed   If you are interested to finding out why I spent 500 Stack Overflow reputation points on one question, stay tuned.  This video will cover three things.   Number one. Why Stack Overflow can be critical for you and your team when searching for solutions for difficult or rare problems.  Number two. Why and when I spent 500 Stack Overflow reputation points on one question.  Number three. How to gain the confidence to ask questions and answer questions on Stack Overflow.   I've led delivery for several large scale production web and mobile apps. Most of them using new or young frameworks. Early adoption of new frameworks comes with their challenges. Often you are the first to find bugs, you are forced to search source code of undocumented features, and you often have a smaller pool of helpful resources and developers to reach out to. I created this channel to be a resource for developers like myself and you. So please, like this video, or subscribe to my channel if you think it's valuable.   Let's talk about number one. Why Stack Overflow can be critical. Stack Overflow, referred to as SO for short, is a question and answer site, and is one of the most trusted online communities for developer. It has over 50 million site visits every month, 51,000 registered developers, and over 19 million answers. You can find help from some of the best developers in the industry on SO. If you ask a common question that is valuable to a lot of developers, you'll get a highly refined answer. Even niched valuable questions receive a lot of attention, and garner a lot of help. Even better, sometimes when you have a question about a specific framework, the creator of the framework may answer the question him or herself, yielding you a high quality and highly accurate answer.   On to number two. Why and when I spent 500 Stack Overflow points, seeking an answer to one of the questions I posted. We were mid sprint. I had a very tight deadline, and a very peculiar bug to fix. Now, mind you, I'm not one of those developers that searches Google and then throws my hands up in the air. There are several things that I do and encourage devs to do before posting a question on SO.   I normally do the following: Number one. Search Google. A quick Google search can sometimes answer your dev question quickly and easily. Number two. Framework documentation. Often times documentation may clearly state an issue, or present a solution. Number three. Breakpoints are stepping through the code. I normally use front end technologies, so Chrome dev tools are most likely being used the majority of time while programming. Mastery of Chrome dev tools from its breakpoint functionality, dom interaction, network tab, and performance utilities, have helped tremendously during development. Number four. Searching SO itself. Many answers can be found by searching SO directly, saving you time and helping you spot a high quality answer. Number five. Consulting another teammate. Walk over and ask another dev or ping someone that you know.   In this case, none of these worked. I was using the d3 library with IONIC, and experienced an issue that I couldn't find a solution for. I implemented my normal debugging routine, and ended up posting a question on Stack Overflow. It didn't gain much attention. I don't think it gained much traction because it was such a rare issue, and would have caused someone to have done quite a bit of digging in order to help. I offered 500 reputation points as a reward for help. This immediately helped my post gain a lot of attention. Someone came to the rescue. It turned out that the problem I was facing was caused by a bug in the framework, centered around single and multi touch.   It was an area that I hadn't dealt with in much detail, so it would've probably taken me weeks to become familiar enough with Touch in order to figure out that it was a framework bug. I didn't have weeks, so this was extremely helpful, and actually saved me a bunch of time, because the developer who identified the bug also offered me an alternative solution that worked. I would've easily paid money for this solution, so SO provided a way for me to pay for a knowledge transfer through the form of SO reputation points.
